scenario: RN home visit, Parkinson's member with falls; wife present, daughter on speakerphone
text: This is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Denise Arroyo]], R N with Cadence, dictating a face to face home visit for [[NAME:Harold Brennan]], date of service [[DATE:October second, twenty twenty six]]. New paragraph. Member is a seventy-eight year old gentleman with Parkinson's disease diagnosed about six years ago, type two diabetes, hypertension and stage three C K D. He was seen in his home at [[ADDRESS:four twelve Willow Bend Drive]] in [[CITY:Kettering]]. His wife [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lorraine]] was present for the whole visit, and their daughter [[RELATIVE_NAME:Kim]], uh, [[RELATIVE_NAME:Kimberly Shaw]], joined on speakerphone partway through. Period. New paragraph. [[NAME:Mister Brennan]] reports two falls since my last visit. The most recent was [[DATE:last Saturday]] night getting up from the recliner to use the bathroom. No head strike, no loss of consciousness. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lorraine]] took him to the E D at [[FACILITY_NAME:Southview Medical Center]] on [[DATE:Sunday]], x-rays negative, discharged same day. The first fall was around [[DATE:the twentieth of September]] and they did not seek care. He is using the walker in the house but not consistently, and he admits he leaves it by the bed. Period. New paragraph. Vitals. Blood pressure one forty two over eighty eight sitting, one twenty eight over seventy six standing, so some orthostatic drop. Pulse seventy four. Fingerstick one sixty one, he had breakfast about two hours prior. Weight one sixty eight. New paragraph. Medications reviewed with [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lorraine]] who fills the pillbox every Sunday. Carbidopa levodopa twenty five one hundred, one and a half tablets three times a day. Metformin five hundred milligrams twice daily. Lisinopril ten milligrams daily. Atorvastatin forty at bedtime. Tamsulosin point four. She said [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Raman]], the neurologist, talked about adding a second Parkinson's medicine but they're waiting until the follow up on [[DATE:November ninth]]. Primary care is [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Alan Whitcomb]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Oakwood Family Practice]], last seen in [[DATE:August]]. New paragraph. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Kim]] raised concern that her mother is getting worn out, she's seventy five herself and has her own back problems. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Kim]] lives in [[CITY:Columbus]] and can come down most weekends. We discussed a referral for in home aide hours through the Medicaid waiver, and I'll send the P T referral for a home safety eval. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lorraine]] asked that we call her cell going forward, that's [[PHONE:nine three seven, five five five, zero one two two]], rather than the house line. Period. New paragraph. Plan. Fall risk education done, night light in the hallway, walker at bedside. Follow up call in one week, next home visit in thirty days. End of dictation.

Patient lives at [[ADDRESS:twenty two hundred Eastlake Avenue, apartment three B]], she's on the third floor and the elevator has been out for about ten days, which is the main reason she's missed her cardiology appointments. Chief complaint, increased leg swelling and shortness of breath when she walks to the kitchen. History of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, last echo showed E F of thirty five percent, atrial fibrillation on apixaban, and hypothyroidism. Exam. Weight is up four pounds from my visit on [[DATE:the sixteenth]]. Assessment, volume overload. Plan, increase furosemide from forty daily to forty twice daily for three days then back to daily, B M P in one week, I'll have the lab come to the house. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Marisol]] will call the Cadence line if weight goes up more than two pounds overnight. Spoke with her cardiologist's office, [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Lindqvist]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Lakeshore Heart Institute]], they'll do a telehealth visit instead. He was admitted to [[FACILITY_NAME:Mercy Ridge Hospital]] on [[DATE:September twenty sixth]] with a COPD exacerbation and discharged on [[DATE:the thirtieth]], um, I'm sorry, discharged [[DATE:October first]]. This is his first visit post discharge. His wife [[RELATIVE_NAME:Gloria]] and their grandson [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tyrese]] were home. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Tyrese]] is nineteen and lives with them. New paragraph. Discharge medications reconciled against the bottles. Prednisone forty milligrams, he has two days left. Azithromycin completed. Trelegy one puff daily, new. Albuterol neb every four hours as needed. Metoprolol succinate twenty five. Aspirin eighty one. Atorvastatin eighty. Sertraline fifty. Discrepancy, the discharge summary lists clopidogrel but he says [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Feldman]], his cardiologist, stopped that a while back. I'll confirm with the cardiology office. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Gloria]] picks up meds at the Walgreens at [[ADDRESS:Ninth and Broad]]. New paragraph. Oxygen, concentrator was delivered by [[ORGANIZATION:Apex Home Medical]] the evening of discharge, portable tanks are supposed to come [[DATE:Thursday]]. Saturation ninety one percent on two liters at rest, eighty seven with walking to the mailbox. Respiratory rate twenty. Lungs with scattered wheezes. He has a follow up with the pulmonologist, [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Ruth Abernathy]], on [[DATE:the fourteenth]] at eleven fifteen, and with his P C P [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Nwosu]] [[DATE:the following week]]. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Gloria]] asked me to email the education handouts to her, address is [[EMAIL:g haynes sixty one at example dot com]], that's [[EMAIL:G H A Y N E S six one]]. New paragraph. Assessment, high readmission risk. Plan, phone check in forty eight hours, home visit again [[DATE:next week]], notify P C P of the medication discrepancy, smoking cessation referral. Their home phone is [[PHONE:six one four, five five five, zero one three nine]]. End dictation.

scenario: Group home visit, adult with Down syndrome and new forgetfulness; sister-guardian present
text: This is [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Paul Ishikawa]], R N, Cadence care management. Face to face visit with [[NAME:Daniel Reyes]] on [[DATE:September twenty ninth, twenty twenty six]], at [[FACILITY_NAME:Maple Grove Residence]], that's the group home on [[ADDRESS:Hawthorne Avenue]] in [[CITY:Springfield]]. Present were [[NAME:Daniel]], his sister [[RELATIVE_NAME:Teresa Reyes]] who is his legal guardian, and the house manager [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Brenda Kolb]]. New paragraph. [[NAME:Daniel]] is a thirty four year old man with Down syndrome, hypothyroidism, obstructive sleep apnea, and obesity. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Teresa]] requested this visit because staff noticed he's more forgetful over the past few months, misplacing his work badge, and he got lost walking back from the bus stop on [[ADDRESS:Hawthorne]] [[DATE:a couple weeks ago]], which never happened before. Given the known association between Down syndrome and early onset Alzheimer's we discussed a referral for a baseline cognitive evaluation. New paragraph. He works three mornings a week, Monday Wednesday and Saturday, bagging groceries at [[EMPLOYER:Harmon's Market]], and he loves it. His supervisor there apparently called [[RELATIVE_NAME:Teresa]] about the badge. New paragraph. Medications per the house M A R. Levothyroxine one hundred twelve micrograms daily, last T S H was two point one in [[DATE:July]]. Melatonin three milligrams. Cetirizine ten. C PAP, staff report he wears it about half the night. Weight two oh four, up six pounds over the last few months. B P one twenty four over seventy eight. New paragraph. Plan. Referral to the memory clinic at [[FACILITY_NAME:Clark County Neurology]], [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Hal Pruitt]]. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Teresa]] wants all appointment calls to go to her, her cell is [[PHONE:nine three seven, five five five, zero one seven one]]. Ask the C PAP supplier about a mask refit. Revisit in one month.

scenario: Wound care physician home visit, diabetic foot ulcer, husband does dressings
text: Doctor [[PROVIDER_NAME:Kenneth Albright]] dictating a home wound care visit. Patient is [[NAME:Margaret]], goes by [[NAME:Peggy]], [[NAME:Sutherland]], date of birth [[DOB:seven twelve nineteen fifty]], Cadence member, seen at her home at [[ADDRESS:eighty one sixty Ridgeline Court, unit two]], in [[CITY:Bend]], [[STATE:Oregon]], [[ZIP:nine seven seven zero two]]. Visit date [[DATE:October fourth]]. Her husband [[RELATIVE_NAME:Walt]] was present and does most of her dressing changes. New paragraph. History. Seventy six year old woman with long standing type two diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease status post left superficial femoral stent, and a chronic ulcer on the plantar surface of the right first metatarsal head, present for roughly four months. She was last seen in the wound clinic at [[FACILITY_NAME:High Desert Regional]] on [[DATE:September nineteenth]] by my partner [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Feliz]]. New paragraph. Wound measures two point one by one point eight by zero point four centimeters, down from two point six by two point two. Moderate serous drainage, granulation base about eighty percent, no tunneling, no erythema beyond one centimeter, no odor. Probe to bone negative. Pedal pulses diminished, dopplerable. New paragraph. Labs, A one C eight point nine in [[DATE:August]], up from seven point nine. [[NAME:Peggy]] admits she's been off her diet since her sister [[RELATIVE_NAME:Joan]] passed in [[DATE:late June]]. Medications, insulin glargine thirty units at night, lispro sliding scale, metformin one thousand twice a day, clopidogrel seventy five, gabapentin three hundred three times daily. New paragraph. Procedure. Sharp debridement of nonviable tissue, she tolerated well. Dressing collagen alginate with foam, offloading boot. [[RELATIVE_NAME:Walt]] was shown again how to apply it. Plan, continue twice weekly dressing changes with home health, the [[ORGANIZATION:Cascade Home Health]] nurse comes Tuesdays and Fridays. Endocrinology referral to tighten control. Return visit [[DATE:two weeks from Monday]]. Vascular follow up with [[PROVIDER_NAME:doctor Imani Brooks]] to reassess flow. If any signs of infection call the clinic at [[PHONE:five four one, five five five, zero one five three]]. End.

Timeline narrative for [[NAME:Yolanda Pierce-Okafor]], prepared by [[CARE_TEAM_MEMBER:Nadia Ferris]], RN, for the [[DATE:October 7]] case review.

[[NAME:Ms. Pierce-Okafor]] first noticed a lump in her left breast around [[DATE:Thanksgiving 2025]] but did not mention it until her mammogram on [[DATE:January 22, 2026]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Fairlawn Imaging]]. Biopsy followed [[DATE:a week later]] ([[DATE:1/29]]) and confirmed invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR positive, HER2 negative, stage IIA. She met with surgical oncologist [[PROVIDER_NAME:Dr. Miriam Castellano]] at [[FACILITY_NAME:Summit Cancer Institute]] on [[DATE:Feb 9]] and had a lumpectomy with sentinel node biopsy on [[DATE:March 2nd]].

Her husband [[RELATIVE_NAME:Desmond]] took leave from [[EMPLOYER:Summit County Library]] for the surgery. Chemo was not recommended after Oncotype (score 14). Radiation, 20 fractions Monday through Friday, ran from [[DATE:April 6]] to [[DATE:May 1]] under [[PROVIDER_NAME:Dr. Pak]]. She developed fatigue and a grade 2 skin reaction but completed all sessions; her sister [[RELATIVE_NAME:Lorna]] drove her most days.

Letrozole 2.5 mg daily was started [[DATE:mid-May]]. In [[DATE:July]] she called the Cadence line reporting joint pain and said she had "taken a break" from the pill for about two weeks. [[PROVIDER_NAME:Dr. Castellano]]'s NP, [[PROVIDER_NAME:Brianne]], switched her to anastrozole on [[DATE:7/24]]. DEXA on [[DATE:8/18]] showed osteopenia (T-score -1.8). She is due for her 6-month surveillance mammogram in [[DATE:early November]].

Other: hypertension (lisinopril 20 mg, BP 132/84 at last visit), pre-diabetes. She is 58 and works from home part-time for [[EMPLOYER:Kessler & Moyer CPAs]]. Preferred contact is email, [[EMAIL:ypo.home@example.org]].
